I just said the other day that, while I realize journal companies need to pay the bills, there are lots of intelligent people who aren't professors that would love to subscribe to academic journals if they had a reasonable fee as opposed to the $1k+ per year cost.

Journal companies don't do much for the community. Here is what I saw as an academic.

  1. I did all the research with money from the government

  2. I paid several hundred dollars to submit my research to a major journal. If I didn't have an academic discount, it would have cost over a thousand dollars.

  3. The journal accepted the paper and asked that I make a few formatting adjustments. I was the one that actually formatted the paper for the journal, they just checked to make sure I was close enough to the style guide.

  4. The journal paid some PhDs to review my work. Note that the PhDs could not recreate my work because the journal had no means of accepting my code or data. The PhDs just read my paper and took my word for it.

  5. The PhDs sent back their comments. 3/5 rejected my paper for reasons that varied from the understandable to "clearly didn't read it."

  6. The journal published it anyway.

Yeah. Journals are all about collecting tons of content under a thin veneer of authenticity so they can turn around and resell "access" to it. These journals are bragging about their 10s of thousands of articles, but a lot of the papers are shit. (I'll reserve judgement on my work. It was a useful trick. It was worth publishing, but maybe not truly new "science.")

I honestly believe that the major Universities should form a collaborative journal and self-publish. The conflict of interest can be managed by leveraging inter-university competition.

It was a great trip. We did our four dives over two days near Runaway Bay. We lucked out and had decent weather. We had two other divers on the boat with us. They each had over 250 dives under their belts.

I'd heard that scuba in Jamaica wasn't that great, due to over fishing. I haven't been anywhere else yet, so I can't really compare. We did see a large variety of fish and other wildlife. We saw a turtle, green spotted eels, a stingray, cuttlefish and other small things like sea cucumbers and such. What amazed me the most was how the scuba operators and the other divers didn't have a problem harassing the wildlife. Our guide manhandled the turtle and the other divers were poking to eels with their GoPro stick to get it to come out. I thought that was odd.

The equipment we rented seemed decent enough, though the bottles fitting was quite corroded. I thought it took a bit more effort to breathe normally compared to the rental equipment we used in our pool lessons. I obviously haven't been out enough to have an educated opinion on that though.

I'm glad it was only a 3 minute boat ride out to our dive spots as the girlfriend gets very sea sick. The operators were very patient and understanding though. She was fine once we got into the water, so we're looking at a location where we can go off the beach for our next trip.

It cost us $300USD each for all four of our referral dives and equipment rental, as well as transportation.

Overall, it was a great experience and would recommend our dive operator and the location.
I just got back from Jamaica and thought I'd tell you guys how it went.
